title: Informer: Beyond Efficient Transformer for Long Sequence Time-Series Forecasting
grouping: No containers: one horizontal chain from the input token stack through embedding, three attention blocks with conv/pool layers between them, to a small output feature map; each part is named in bold below it.
shapes_depth: Everything is drawn in 3-D perspective: the input is a stack of thin green slices split into 'Scalar' and 'Stamp' rows spanning T = t to T = t + D_x; dashed projection lines fan from it to two long bars (blue Conv1d, grey Embedding, each d × L) summed at a green sphere with a plus. Each attention block is a translucent beige box holding several red head slabs (n-heads, k), followed by blue and cyan slabs for Conv1d and MaxPool1d with 'padding=2' written diagonally along them. Block sizes shrink from L to L/2 to L/4, and those dimension labels are written along the boxes' edges; the output is a small purple box 'Feature Map' (d × L/4). Teal arrows connect stages.
proposed_highlight: The distilling operation is the subject: the conv/pool slabs between attention blocks are the only blue/cyan elements, and their effect is shown by the shrinking size of the next block.
lesson: Show sequence-length halving by drawing each successive attention block as a smaller 3-D box with L, L/2, L/4 written on its length edge, so the distilling is read from the geometry before any label.
notes: Venue from Semantic Scholar (AAAI); year = arXiv preprint year (2012.07436).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
